issue.title: Restore `feature` as an agent-creatable task type in every project
issue.description: The builtin `feature` task type is agent-creatable everywhere by default: no machine-global `bead.task_types` entry suppresses it, the `sase` project no longer carries a re-enable override, and the shipped `create_refusal` copy no longer names one machine's policy.

issue.title: Drop the machine-global `feature` disable from chezmoi
issue.description: global-default: delete the `bead.task_types` block from the chezmoi-managed `home/dot_config/sase/sase.yml` so no machine-global layer turns `agent_creatable` off for `builtin@feature`. This phase's commit runs chezmoi's own `after` hook, which redeploys `~/.config/sase/sase.yml` and makes the change live for every project on the machine.

issue.title: Neutralize the builtin refusal copy and retire the sase re-enable override
issue.description: sase-cleanup: in the sase repo, rewrite the `create_refusal` copy in `_feature_spec()` so it stops asserting that feature beads belong only to SASE, delete the now-dead `use: builtin@feature` override from `sase/sase.yml`, extend the builtin copy test, and regenerate `sase/task_types.json`. Gated on `global-default` because that regeneration reads the live machine-global config layer.

payload.entry: Deleted the bead.task_types block (lines 3-7) from chezmoi's home/dot_config/sase/sase.yml, removing the machine-global builtin@feature agent_creatable:false override. Verified: grep for builtin@feature in the chezmoi repo returns no matches, grep -c '^bead:' on the file returns 0, and the file still parses as valid YAML. No other lines touched. Left chezmoi/apply/update untouched per plan D3 — redeploy happens via chezmoi's own commit_hooks.after when this phase is committed. No epic-symbol leftovers (sase bead epic-symbols sase-tn.1 reported none).

Updated feature refusal copy, removed the redundant SASE project feature override, regenerated sase/task_types.json, and verified with pytest tests/task_types/test_builtin.py, git diff --check, sase bead task-type list -a, just check, and sase bead epic-symbols sase-tn.2.

VERIFIED (step 1 — both phases, against source and commits, not reports):

sase-tn.1 (chezmoi, no commit in this repo): the top-level `bead:` block is gone from
`home/dot_config/sase/sase.yml` in the chezmoi source, `grep -rn builtin@feature` over the
whole chezmoi repo returns nothing, and the deployed `~/.config/sase/sase.yml` matches the
source — so chezmoi's `commit_hooks.after` redeploy really did fire. chezmoi's worktree is
clean.

sase-tn.2 (5ca05f6a5): the diff is exactly the four planned paths. `_feature_spec()` carries
the D2 copy verbatim; `sase/sase.yml`'s `bead.task_types` list now starts at `flag` with the
`use: builtin@feature` entry and its two comment lines deleted; `tests/task_types/test_builtin.py`
gained the banned-substring loop and the PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP assertion; `sase/task_types.json`
changed only inside the `feature` object (source project->builtin, package project->sase,
digest 9445f917->c461e1e8, new create_refusal), with agent_creatable already true.

Live behavior confirms both phases composed: `sase bead task-type show feature --json` reports
agent_creatable true and provenance.source builtin/package sase; `sase bead task-type list -a`
shows feature agent-creatable while flag and github stay uncreatable; the `Feature` row and the
`sase/memory/task_types/feature.md` strand are present. `sase validate` passes all seven checks
including `init memory --check`, and `tests/task_types/` is 43 passed. Grepping the repo for
`machine-global`, `feature bead only`, `only in SASE`, and `builtin@feature` finds no stale
policy text outside the test's own banned-substring list. Neither child bead nor the epic
carried any PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note.

INTEGRATED (step 2): the epic's commit is HEAD and equals origin/master, so nothing landed
after it. The one commit that landed inside the epic's window — 50d9c3bc2 (12:57), which trimmed
the generated agent instruction files and reworked src/sase/main/init_memory/ rendering — sits
directly under 5ca05f6a5 and does not conflict: `sase memory init --check --diff` plans no
changes at all, so the epic's regenerated snapshot is consistent with the new renderers. No
other code in the repo duplicated or contradicted what this epic added.

FOLLOW-UP: filed sase-tq (task(memory), small, ready, linked related->sase-tn). actstat and
bob-cli each ran `sase init memory` at 13:02, one minute after 5ca05f6a5, using an installed
`sase` that had phase 1 but not phase 2. Both therefore committed a half-updated `feature`
snapshot: agent_creatable/source/package correct, but digest still 9445f917 and create_refusal
still the retired copy that names one machine's config layer. The epic plan's D4 deferred this
regeneration out of every phase on purpose, and running it rewrites files under `sase/memory/`
in two other projects, which needs the project owner's go-ahead rather than a plan's
authorization — so it is recorded rather than done here. `sase validate` in each repo reports
the drift and names the fix, so nothing fails silently. Nothing else was proposed and nothing
was declined.
